messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — planning to publish the Py/TS SDK canary during today's change window at 14:30 PT. Will tag canary and push a docs note.

maria: SG. Which versions are we publishing as canary?

alex: py -> 0.14.0-canary.1, ts -> 0.14.0-canary.1. npm tag = canary, pypi pre-release.

jamie: FYI we still have the sync client deprecation note pending. Should we include it in release notes or separate?

alex: Include short deprecation warning in SDK changelog + a separate email to enterprise customers. Link in changelog to migration guide.

deploy-bot: publish job queued: sdk-ts-canary #1806324000 by alex. Status: queued -> running.

alex: Publishing commands for posterity:
```bash
# TS
npm version 0.14.0-canary.1 --no-git-tag-version
npm publish --tag canary
# PY
python -m build
TWINE_USERNAME=redwood TWINE_PASSWORD=$TWINE_TOKEN twine upload dist/* --repository testpypi
```

sophie: Can we gate the canary on the integration smoke tests? I can trigger the suite after publish.

tyler: Yes — we'll keep production traffic on stable. Canary only used for internal smoke + a couple of early-adopter orgs. If smoke fails we rollback canary and revoke tags.

maria: Also please add checksum/sha in the release thread so infra can validate artifacts.

alex: Good call. I'll paste shas once build finishes.

deploy-bot: publish job succeeded: sdk-ts-canary #1806324000. Artifact: @redwood/sdk@0.14.0-canary.1.

alex: TS publish ✅. Pushing PY now to test PyPI then will mirror to prod PyPI when canary checks pass. SHA256: 3f7b9c9a... (will attach full in release note).

jamie: Running smoke tests -> starting now. Test run id: smoke-1806324.

jamie: smoke: embeddings endpoint + auth flow passed; streaming tests flaky (2/5 failures) — investigating.

sophie: Flaky streaming could be due to changed serializer in TS. I can repro locally. Suggest hold on prod PyPI mirror until we confirm.

alex: Agreed. Hold on prod PyPI. We'll cut a rollback plan if streaming regressions persist.

maria: For rollback: steps to unpublish canary tag from npm and delete testpypi artifacts, plus update changelog that canary was withdrawn. Add note for partners channel.

tyler: Write rollback steps here so ops can run if needed:
```bash
# npm unpublish (canary tag only)
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk canary || true
# revoke PyPI artifacts (support ticket to pypi)
# update changelog + set npm tag to previous canary target if needed
```

alex: OK creating release draft now: https://redwood-internal/release-notes/sdk/0.14.0-canary.1 (private). I'll include deprecation blurb: 
"Deprecation: the legacy sync client (redwood-sync) will be deprecated in next stable. See migration guide: https://redwood-internal/docs/migrate-sync"

jamie: ETA on fix for streaming?

sophie: Found root cause — header encoding when using gRPC fallback. Patch ready, will open PR in 20m.

alex: If PR lands and CI green within 45m we proceed to mirror to prod PyPI and publish release notes. If not, we withdraw canary and re-run tests after fix.

deploy-bot: PR #1289 merged by sophie. CI: passed.

jamie: Re-running smoke -> all green now (streaming 5/5).

alex: Great. Proceeding to mirror PY to prod and final publish.

deploy-bot: pypi mirror initiated by alex.

maria: Reminder: update docs landing page and add deprecation banner. I'll file a docs PR after you confirm final version.

alex: Done. Release notes published, changelog entry added, deprecation note included. Announcing in #devex and emailing enterprise list.

tyler: Post-mortem notes: add automated streaming regression test to prevent this slipping. I'll create a ticket.

alex: Thanks everyone. TL;DR: canary -> failed then fixed -> mirrored to prod. Legacy sync deprecation communicated. Rollback plan documented if anything else pops. :tada:
